label: paragraph_title
text: LAWN TENNIS FINALS.

label: table
paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: At Wimbledon, in the British Open Lawn Tennis Championships, (final, men's doubles), Jean Borotra and Rene Lacoste beat Hennessey and Casey, 6-4, 11-9, 4-6, 1-6, 6-3.

label: text
text: This doubles was a magnificent match. France was in the ascendant at the start but the Americans fought splendidly. Casey's terrific service was a feature: he also showed surprising strength overhead. The Frenchmen covered the court better than the Americans, who however won two sets by sheer hard hitting. In the deciding set Borotra was superb and no ball was too far for him to get at; his anticipations were uncannily accurate, and his kills untakeable. Hennessey played well but appeared to tire towards the close.

label: text
text:
In the final of the mixed doubles
Borotra and Mlle. Suzanne
Lenglen heat De Morpurgo and
Miss Ryan, 6-3, 6-3.

label: text
text: Wimbledon concluded 'in fine weather. Borotra' and Mlle. Lenglen won the two opening games easily, mainly through the former's accurate overhead smashing, but lost next three. The sixth game went to the French pair. Suzanne was playing magnificently and then the French pair were in irresistible form and secured the set.

label: text
text: In the second set the French team work was superb. After each side had won a game, the French went to 4-1. De Morpurgo and Miss Ryan could not cope with the splendid variety of shots of the French pair.

label: text
text: From the following list it will be seen that with the exception of the mixed doubles in which Suzanne Lenglen shared the honours with Miss Ryan. the French visitors annexed every championship:—

label: text
text: Men's Singles: R. Lacoste beat J. Borotra (holder) both of France.

label: text
text: Men's Doubles: Borotra and Lacoste (France) beat John Hennessey and Ray Casey (U.S.A.)

label: text
text: Ladies' Singles: Mlle. Suzanne Lenglen (France) beat Miss Joan Fry (Britain).

label: text
text: Ladies' Doubles: Mlle. Lenglen (France) and Miss Ryan (U.S.A.) beat Mrs. Bridge and Mrs. Meilquham.

label: text
text: Mixed Doubles: Borotra and Mlle. Lēnglen (France) bent De Morpurgo (Italy) and Miss Ryan (U.S.A.)

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: At Wimbledon, under a cloudy sky, a large attendance, including His Majesty the King, saw De Morpurgo and Miss Ryan beat J. H. P. Wheatley and Mrs. Lambert Chambers 9-7, 6-4. The British players were within one point of the first set at 6-5. Wheatley played splendid all-round tennis, but showed a tendency to double-fault. Miss Ryan was excellent at the net, and Mrs. Lambert Chambers was more successful on the baseline. De Morpurgo's ground work and Wheatley's smashing were features of a brilliant second set.

label: text
text: In the All England Plate final, the Hungarian Kehrling beat the Englishman. It George 6-3, 6-4.

label: text
text: Finals will be played Monday, to obviate Porotra contesting three finals in one day.

label: text
text: In the final of the Ladies' Doubles, Mlla. Tenglen and Miss Ryan beat Mrs. Bridge and Mrs. McIlquham 6-2, 6-2.

label: text
text: The Men's Singles final was won by R. Lacoste, who beat Jean Borotn 6-3, 6-3, 4-6, 8-6.

label: text
text: Borotra lost the title to a better tactician. With the exception of infrequent hits out Incoste's very accurate baselining kept the holder from the net. Borotra was erratic at the opening, often mistiming, whereas Incoste was very steady, particularly on his back hand. Borotra several times footnulated in the first set.

label: text
text: The second was marked by brilliant rallies which ended by superb passing shots.

label: text
text: Borotra, in serving, again holed the net, but the ball did not go through. The net was changed at the end of the set. The champion recovered last year's dash in the third set though he was kept running on the baseline in the fourth. Lacoste continued to exploit baselining with almost mathematical accuracy and led 4-1. The champion drew level at 4 all but Lacoste won against service then on his own for the match.

label: text
text: ANNUAL CRICKET MATCH YESTERDAY.

label: text
text: Very little has come out in the last mail or two to indicate the composition of the teams, but from the results cabled by Reuter, Cambridge seem to be the more formidable.

label: text
text: Yesterday the annual cricket match between Oxford and Cambridge Universities began at Lord's but no score has come through.

label: text
text: BLUES AT LORD'S.

label: text
text: To date 86 matches have been played; Cambridge have won 41, Oxford 36 and 9 have been left drawn.

label: text
text: Names which have been given prominence to date include the awarding of a Blue to K. S. Duleepsinjhi (Cambridge), who is a nephew of the famous Ranjil.

label: text
text: C. T. Bennett is the Light Blue captain and other old Blues whose names have cropped up in the cables are H. J. Enthoven, L. G. Crawley, E. W. Dawson, H. M. Austin and R. J. O. Meyer.

label: text
text: T. E. S. Francis, a Cambridge senior, has been playing well this year.

label: text
text: Oxford freshmen who have done well so far are E. R. T. Holmes (Malvern) and G. W. F. Lyon (Brighton). J. L. Guise is the Dark Blue skipper: other Old Blues whose names have been noticed are C. H. Taylor. E. P. Hewetson and T. B. Raikes. G. B. Legger, a senior, made top-score against the M.C.C. and I. A. W. Gilliatt, another senior, has also been prominent.

label: text
text: In mail week it was announced that J. V. Richardson (Uppingham and Brasenose) had been given his Blue.

label: paragraph_title
text: LIEUT. LIVOCK.

label: paragraph_title
text: KEEPS WICKET FOR MIDDLESEX.

label: text
text: INTERPORT CRICKETER.

label: text
text: Flight Lieut. G. E. Livock, R.A.F., who played for Malaya against Hongkong and Shanghai in the triangular interport cricket matches here last year, has turned out for Middlesex at Home this season.

label: text
text: Prior to coming to Hongkong on the seaplane carrier Pegasus, Lieut. Livock already had a big reputation as he had. "kept" wicket for Lord Cowdray's XI against an England XI which included some of the best players in the Old Country.

label: text
text: In the interport series he batted first for Malaya. Though his average was not big his batting was certainly very impressive and his work behind the sticks was brilliant. Against Kowloon he made a century. When Mr. Ezra Abraham. Vice-President of the K.C.C: presented him with a bat, Lieut. Livock hinted that he would have preferred a golf club.

label: text
text: However, his inclusion in the Lord's team seems to indicate that he has not deserted the summer game. A Home paper, in mail week, mentions him as an amateur from Chiswick. He was ninth on the batting list and scored 20 not out after some of the opening batsmen had failed. Only the first day's play was given and Warwickshire, who were playing at Lord's had only started their innings so it is not known if he did anything spectacular. According to a Reuter cable at the time, Middlesex eventually won the match.

label: text
text: Lieut. Livock's progress now that he is at Home will be watched with interest by cricketers who have seen him in the Far East.

label: text
text: London, July 4.—At Glenegles in a thousand-guineer professional golf tournament, the final, over thirty-six holes was won by A. Compston (North Manchester), who beat Abe Mitchell by one hole. Reuter.

text: Moscow, July 5. — Chicherin has sent Mr. Hodgson, the British Charge d'Affaires at Moscow, a Note protesting against the trial at Shanghai and demanding the release of Dosser, maintaining that documents alleged to belong to him are forgeries.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEXT TESTS.

label: text
text: HUBERT ASHTON TO BE CAPTAIN?

label: paragraph_title
text: NEWS FROM HOME.

label: text
text: Hubert Ashton, the former Cambridge University captain, is likely to succeed A. E. R. Gilligan as England's cricket captain for the next series of Test Matches with Australia, in England, in 1926, says a Home paper writer in mail week.

label: text
text: Ashton is not at present in England but he is expected to be Home for the next season, as is C. H. Gibson, the Light Blue (1920-1921) bowler who was chosen to go to Australia last year but had to cry off.

label: text
text:
It is hinted that the strain which is now preventing Gilligan from bowling may effect the selectors' decision. Ashton is one of three brothers who led the Light Blues in successive years. When at Cambridge in 1921, the year of Warwick Armstrong's conquest, he distinguished himself in all the matches in which he played against the Australians and was a member of A. C. MacLaren's XI, which inflicted the first check on the Australians.
The same writer mentions Ashton's superb example in the field and that his strong back play is the most likely to demoralise a bowler like Grimmelt who skittled out the M.C.C. team in the very last Test Match.

label: paragraph_title
text: FRENCH RETIRING.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: Paris, July 6.

label: text
text: A War Ministry communiqué referring to “pessimistic reports on recent military events in Eastern Morocco in the direction of Tazza,” says that “certain loyally tribes partly failed us, opening a breach in the first line of defence, through which the Riffs passed and attacked our regular troops, who are now taking up the best positions to repel the enemy. Public opinion must not be disturbed by these inevitable episodes in colonial warfare.” The communiqué refers to the difficulties of the French forces, owing to the improvement in the enemy's numbers, equipment, and tactics compared with ten years ago and adds “Their attacks are more frequent, and better co-ordinated on a wider front. They are constructing trenches, dug-outs, and barbed wire entanglements, whereas the tactics of modern armies, concentrating to strike decisive blows, if employed too systematically, are bound to result in the disaffection of abandoned loyal tribes, with a consequent infiltration of enemy contingents. We must not be surprised or alarmed if, on a vast front difficulties should lead locally to retirements, regroupings, and concentrations of our forces that, however, prepare the way to more vigorous counterblows.”

label: paragraph_title
text: France and Spain.

label: text
text: The newspapers publish interviews with M. Malvy; who is negotiating with the Spanish Government at Madrid, declaring that a complete Franco-Spanish agreement has been established and stating that a peace offer has been drafted and will be offered to Abd El Krim when the French Government has concurred in the details.

label: text
text: According to Le Journal's Madrid correspondent, under the peace offer to Abd El Krim the Riffs will be assured full freedom for development under the nominal sovereignty of the Sultan of Morocco within frontiers still to be determined.

label: text
text: Some surrenders of arms will be demanded as a symbolic act, but not the surrender of the whole of Abd El Krim's war material.

label: text
text: The terms, however, do not correspond with Abd El Krim's demands.

label: text
text: Paris, July 6.

label: text
text: The Ministry of War denies the pessimistic messages concerning Riffan infiltrations which are “but the normal consequence of singular conditions in the operations.” Regular troops are taking steps to make the Riffans pay dearly for their attacks against several local tribes which partly went over to the enemy after having gallantly resisted repeated Riffan attacks.
